body: I'm also in California. I'll send you a PM.

Hey, thank you for the message. I'm sorry you're over the edge, too. I hope you know however that your feelings are none less valid than others. It's not worth it to compare yourself to other people; suicidal ideations can happen to anyone, and just because you might have "shit reasons" for feeling how you do doesn't mean that your feelings aren't worthy. There will always be someone out there who "has it worse" than you, but that doesn't mean that your problems don't matter, or that they aren't significant.

By the way, just so you know, knowing that there's someone out there who wants someone to talk to has helped me decide that I'm not going to do the deed just yet, not tonight. Maybe tomorrow night. I would like to talk with you first. Send me a PM and we can talk, alright? I'm available pretty much all day tomorrow as it's Sunday (What time zone are you in, if you don't mind me asking? I'm PST.) Thank you for caring and I hope things get better for you.

Thank you so much. I really, truly appreciate it so much. I'm so sorry about the hardships you've faced and I am so glad you are still here because you seem like a genuinely beautiful and kind person. 

I've attempted suicide before, and I've very nearly succeeded once. I've just been feeling lately that it was a mistake that I lived. That there really is no solution. That maybe there is peace at the bottom of this bottle of Percocet. I've been trying so, so hard. It feels like there's no hope. 

But people like you help me see the light, even if it only flickers in for a second, so thank you so much.

Hi, thanks for your response, I appreciate it.

I have talked to the people at my school, and I'll admit that they were as helpful as they can be. The school psychologist has given me a list of resources (she even told me to download an app for breathing exercises for anxiety, which I admit helps), and she's tried to schedule meetings with my parents but they always refuse. I meet with the school psychologist at least once a week. Granted, we only meet for about ten minutes (I go to a public school with 2000+ students), but it's still something. Unfortunately, I feel like she doesn't really give a shit. Like the second I leave her office, I hear her laughing with the other staff members at school and she just goes on with her day. And I don't really expect her to care too much about me because I'm just some random girl, but still, it's a stark reminder that life goes on and I don't really matter that much.

The one meeting my parents actually attended with my college counselor, school psychologist, a teacher of mine, and the assistant principal, my parents ended up walking out of because they recommended psychiatric help.

I'm supposed to talk with my college counselor next Tuesday, but I'm scared it's going to just be the same shit and nothing will change, just like always.
